title: Transactions (advanced)
summary: All-or-nothing changes: commit, rollback and why two writes must share one transaction.
body:
All-or-nothing changes: commit, rollback and why two writes must share one transaction.

Why it matters: A transfer is two writes. If only one lands, money is created or destroyed. A transaction makes the pair atomic: both commit, or a failure rolls both back.

SQL ↔ ORM: SQLAlchemy Session.begin() context. Prisma $transaction([...]) or $transaction(async (tx) => …). SQL BEGIN … COMMIT (the lab wraps your script for you).
why: A transfer is two writes. If only one lands, money is created or destroyed. A transaction makes the pair atomic: both commit, or a failure rolls both back.
objectives: Group related writes in one transaction.
Python: `with Session(engine) as s, s.begin():` — Prisma: `$transaction` — SQL: BEGIN/COMMIT.
pitfalls: Two separate sessions/calls for one logical change.
Using the global client inside a Prisma interactive transaction.
mappingNotes: SQLAlchemy Session.begin() context. Prisma $transaction([...]) or $transaction(async (tx) => …). SQL BEGIN … COMMIT (the lab wraps your script for you).
teachAlong: Cause: All-or-nothing changes: commit, rollback and why two writes must share one transaction.
Effect: run the exercise and read the gate's rule ids.

exercise.prompt: Answer every question — each wrong option explains why it is wrong.

questions.prompt: You move money between two accounts with Prisma. Which call keeps both updates atomic?

options.text: Two awaited prisma.account.update() calls in a row
options.why: Each call is its own transaction — if the second fails, the first is already committed.

options.text: prisma.$transaction([debit, credit]) or an interactive prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => …)

options.why: Promise.all only runs them concurrently; they are still separate transactions.

questions.prompt: Inside prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => …) the credit throws. What happens to the debit?

options.text: It is rolled back together with everything else in the callback

options.why: The interactive transaction only commits when the callback resolves; a throw rolls it all back.
Prisma does not retry; you decide (e.g. on serialization failures).

questions.prompt: Inside an interactive transaction you call prisma.user.update (not tx.user.update). Why is that a bug?

options.text: It runs on a different connection, outside the transaction
It is fine — Prisma detects the surrounding transaction
options.why: Only the `tx` client is bound to the transaction; the global client is not.
It compiles fine — which is exactly why this bug is easy to ship.
